newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel up on Framatome merger study.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel up on Framatome merger study.

text.p: Shares in engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom were up on the Paris bourse on Friday after the group said that it and its venture partner, Britain's GEC, were studying the possibility of a merger of GEC Alsthom with French state-controlled nuclear reactor builder Framatome.
Alcatel shares ticked up on the news and were trading 1.70 francs, or 0.44 percent higher, at 392.50 francs at 1014 GMT. The bourse's CAC index was down 0.14 percent at the same time.
"Obviously Alcatel has wanted to do this for a long time," said analyst Christopher Tucker at Paribas Capital Markets. "There's industrial logic behind the deal."
"Most of Alcatel's big competitors have the capability to offer nuclear as well as traditional power plants. This would allow Alcatel to compete on the same footing," Tucker said.
The statements issued on Friday by the French government, which gave its blessing to such a study after having long opposed it, and Alcatel gave no financial information.
Analysts said it was too early to estimate the financial implications of such a deal.
